protocol: per shape: warmup both arms, then reps x (fp8blk timed, q8_0 timed) INTERLEAVED inside the rep loop so both arms share one clock/thermal regime; median of reps; flock /tmp/gpu5090.lock. Weight operand is the SAME logical weight for both arms: the e4m3 codes are the source, and the Q8_0 slab is produced from them by the merged ARM B' device dequant, i.e. the actual floor path this kernel competes with.
shapes: the 27B's own, read from /root/models/qwen36-27b-fp8 safetensors headers
thermal: m=512 leg 43C->54C, sm 180->1725 MHz (idle-start, ramping); m=6257 leg sustained

why: the end-to-end 27B pp number cannot answer the perf question. The kernel's operand is made resident by the MEMRA_PP_FP8 stash, which DUPLICATES every F8-origin projection on top of the resident Q8_0 and so needs a VRAM budget; at the measured ~355 MiB of e4m3 per 27B layer the 3072 MB that fits beside a 27 GB model covers a prefix of ~8.6 of 64 layers. ARM A has no such cap: its scale-fold makes the operand blk=None, which admits it to the MEMRA_ST_E4M3 one-copy arm (no duplicate, no budget, all 64 layers). So pp512 mmq-vs-arma is NOT like-for-like coverage, and the kernel itself has to be measured directly.

sweep: FP8_MMQ_X token tile (build-time, MEMRA_MMQ_X_FP8). FP8_MMQ_Y is NOT swept: a static_assert pins it to 128 because mmq_y == the scale block edge is what makes the scale row equal blockIdx.x and collapses the whole scale fetch to two scalar loads per 256-k iteration.
note: kernel-check ALL GREEN at every X — the tile geometry does not touch exactness
only the tiny 5120->1024 shape gains (1.194x) — that is the one shape whose out_f=1024 gives just 8 row tiles, so a smaller token tile buys CTAs; every real shape loses ~23%
best of the sweep on the two largest shapes (down_proj 0.990, o_proj 0.956) but still AT OR BELOW the floor, and it collapses the small shape to 0.512x

verdict: NEGATIVE ON PERF, at every 27B projection shape and at both m=512 and m=6257: the per-block FP8 MMQ tile runs 0.81x-0.94x the Q8_0 MMQ floor it was written to beat (X=128, the default and the sweep winner; X=64/32/256 are all worse or equal). The exactness result stands independently — kernel-check is ALL GREEN at every tile size — but the arm does not clear its own reason for existing.

mechanism: both arms land at 105-127 TFLOP against the 381-TF class the f8f6f4 MMA is capable of, so NEITHER is MMA-bound and the MMA-shape advantage this kernel was built on (e4m3 x e4m3 native, weight tile is a pure byte copy, zero decode) cannot pay. The two arms move the same weight bytes per output (1 byte/weight for e4m3 vs Q8_0's 34 B/32 = 1.0625 B/weight, i.e. only a 6% read advantage), so there is no bandwidth win to collect either. What differs is per-tile work: the Q8_0 tile's int8 MMA accumulates in s32 with ONE f32 fold at the end, while this tile carries an f32 accumulator and folds (s_blk * dB) per k-block. The scale-row hoist already reduced that to two scalar loads per 256-k iteration, so the remaining cost is the f32 accumulate/fold itself — structural to per-block FP8, not a tuning miss.
